body: Interestingly, when -u NORC is not specified, it takes until a screen resize or backgrounding to get to the state I described
Can you please post a backtrace using the steps from https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki/Development-tips#backtrace-linux
Not sure I understand. My ulimit for core file size is unlimited, but there is no core file. The segfault only happens when I exit vim, could that keep it from creating one?
@oatmealraisin No. What makes you think it is a segfault? What is the exact error you see?

> My ulimit for core file size is unlimited

You must run `ulimit -c unlimited` in the current shell. It doesn't persist. Please do that, then provoke the segfault, and it should produce a core somewhere. If the `core` file doesn't appear in the current directory, https://stackoverflow.com/a/18368068/152142 may help (or Arch linux wiki, I guess).

@oatmealraisin great, thanks! Would be even better if you could follow the steps at https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki/Development-tips#backtrace-linux

tl;dr:

    gdb path/to/nvim path/to/core 2>&1 | tee backtrace.txt
    thread apply all bt full

then upload backtrace.txt to https://gist.github.com. I promise I'll stop pestering you after that :)

Unfortunately, the core files were formatted an odd way that gdb didn't like, sorry. [This](https://gist.github.com/anonymous/81a2cd97aaf334b70721ba9409de80c3) is as close as I can find. The core dumps are being handled by systemd, these were found in /var/lib/systemd/coredump as an lz4 archive. After decompression, I fed these into the gdb call provided in the wiki. Hope this helps!

Looks like `grid->row` is increased too much. Can you test the following patch for the resizing problem?

```diff
diff --git a/src/nvim/tui/tui.c b/src/nvim/tui/tui.c
index 8e0e905bc..1a65a78cb 100644
--- a/src/nvim/tui/tui.c
+++ b/src/nvim/tui/tui.c
@@ -467,7 +467,7 @@ static void final_column_wrap(UI *ui)
   UGrid *grid = &data->grid;
   if (grid->col == ui->width) {
     grid->col = 0;
-    if (grid->row < ui->height) {
+    if (grid->row < MIN(ui->height, grid->height-1)) {
       grid->row++;
     }
   }

```
Your second backtrace could hint that `grid->cells` was deallocated twice.
Perhaps this patch helps a bit?

```diff
diff --git a/src/nvim/ugrid.c b/src/nvim/ugrid.c
index 2b5e96ee6..e0880b4c7 100644
--- a/src/nvim/ugrid.c
+++ b/src/nvim/ugrid.c
@@ -135,6 +135,7 @@ static void destroy_cells(UGrid *grid)
       xfree(grid->cells[i]);
     }
     xfree(grid->cells);
+    grid->cells = NULL;
   }
 }
```

@oni-link @justinmk I should have tested this first, but the error isn't reproducable on terminator, or while using tmux. I'm running on Wayland, so I'm willing to chalk this up to Xwayland. Feel free to close this, or I can continue debugging for you. Thanks again for the help.

issue.title: Segfault when resizing terminal to small sizes

labels.name: bug-crash
labels.description: issue reporting a crash or segfault

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
<!-- Before reporting: search existing issues and check the FAQ. -->

- `nvim --version`: 0.2.3-24-gd9b3ebfed (also tested on 0.2.2 release)
- Vim (version: ) behaves differently? Yes
- Operating system/version: Arch Linux, Xfce 4.12
- Terminal name/version: Terminator 1.91
- `$TERM`: xterm-256color

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`

See below

### Actual behaviour

Neovim crashes with a segmentation fault

### Expected behaviour

No crash

---

First one occurs when changing the width of the terminal to less than 5 *columns*. Crashes in `ugrid_put`, caused by an out-of-bounds access on `grid->cells[grid->row]` (when `grid->row == grid->height`).
